rationale: This workflow is a manually triggered (workflow_dispatch) deployment to staging, not a build/test workflow. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-cache experiment (batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9) requires a repeated dependency-fetching step with a lockfile-keyed install; this workflow has no npm/go install step, so the cache precondition is not met and adding actions/cache would be an unrelated change. P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is expressly contraindicated for release/deployment work, so canceling superseded runs is unsafe here. There is no matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST), no schedule (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE/P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE), and a single job (P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST). P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT requires representative successful-duration history, but the repository context labels the CI history as not_a_measured_baseline/historical_context_only, and observed runs vary widely (~5-14 min), so a derived timeout risks cutting off valid slow deployments (contraindication: valid slow runs exceed the limit). No evidence-supported change safely fits this deployment workflow without weakening it or adding unsupported behavior.
